caption:
How to handle a maybe RSVP for your wedding: give it a date, then follow up kindly.
Entry 03 of Norah's Notebook: a polite follow-up ladder, a message to copy, and why twenty percent is a rule of thumb, not a fact.
Fiction: Norah and the couple are invented. The tips are real.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment: Copy, paste, send for a maybe: "Maybe is fine! The caterer needs numbers soon. Could you let us know by the deadline?" The polite ladder: a short nudge a week before the deadline, one personal message a week after, then a call (The Knot guide; Joy, 2025; Emily Post, 2008). Message each person on their own, not in the group chat. The twenty percent decline figure is a rule of thumb with no published sample, and guides disagree (The Knot; Zola, 2026). Fiction: Mara, Eli and Norah are invented; the tips are real. Norah is AI-generated. Screens shown are real Wedillybird screens (demo data).
comment_bait: When a guest says maybe, do you count it as a yes or a no?

sources.fact: Send a nudge about one week before the deadline and a second note a week after; avoid group chats, mass emails and public posts that tag non-responders; phone silent guests after the deadline
sources.title: When Should You Send a Wedding RSVP Reminder? Wording to Know

sources.fact: Wait about a week after the deadline; keep reminders friendly; tell guests the date vendors need final numbers; ask close family or the wedding party to help
sources.title: How to Set Perfect Wedding RSVP Deadlines

sources.fact: Check in as the cut-off approaches with a short message that states the deadline; a fiance(e), parents or attendants can make the calls; accommodate late replies where possible
sources.title: Inside Weddings: Handling Your Guests With Grace

sources.fact: Venues and caterers need real final headcounts; the RSVP deadline sits before the vendor's headcount date so there is time to chase
sources.title: How to Set Perfect Wedding RSVP Deadlines

sources.fact: Many wedding professionals use about 20% declines as a starting estimate, adjusted for time of year and travel distance; no source gives a universal rate (another Knot guide says 10-20%; Zola expects about 50% attendance for destination weddings)
sources.title: Plan for This Percentage of Guests to RSVP 'Yes'; The Ultimate Destination Wedding Checklist
sources.date: Knot: undated (search extract); Zola destination checklist: 2026-02-05
